short_description.id: Minairó adalah makhluk mungil pekerja keras dari Pyrenees Katalonia yang disimpan ribuan di dalam tabung jarum dan selalu menuntut pekerjaan, membawa kemakmuran bagi pemiliknya.
short_description.en: The minairó is a tiny hard-working being of the Catalan Pyrenees, kept by the thousand in a needle case and always demanding work, which brings its owner prosperity.

long_description.id: Minairó, juga diablorí di Katalonia atau zaingorriak di negeri Basque, adalah makhluk sangat kecil yang di desa-desa Pyrenees disimpan ribuan dalam tabung jarum. Mereka berasal dari St John's-wort yang tumbuh di gua dalam yang dijaga raksasa dan naga dan hanya dapat diambil tengah malam Santo Yohanes. Mereka mendengung seperti lebah atau nyamuk dan begitu keluar menuntut, "Apa yang kita kerjakan? Apa yang kita katakan?"
long_description.en: The minairó, called diablorí by some in Catalonia and zaingorriak in the Basque lands, is a tiny being kept by the thousand in a needle case in Pyrenean villages. They come from St John's-wort, which grows in deep caves guarded by giants and dragons and can only be taken at midnight on St John's Day. They buzz like bees or mosquitoes and on coming out demand, 'What shall we do? What shall we say?'

long_description.id: Pemilik tabung menjadi makmur, tetapi bila pembukanya tidak segera memberi tugas, mereka bisa membunuhnya; banyak hamparan batu longsoran di Pyrenees konon hasil kerja mereka ketika tabung terbuka tak sengaja. Di negeri Basque, roh kecil serupa disebut mamarroak atau galtzagorriak dan melindungi keluarga.
long_description.en: Owners of the case prospered, but if the opener did not give them a task at once they might kill him; many Pyrenean screes are said to be their work when a case was opened by accident. In the Basque Country similar small spirits are the mamarroak or galtzagorriak, who protect the family.

role.en: Do any work for their owner.

famous_for.id: "Apa yang kita kerjakan? Apa yang kita katakan?"
famous_for.en: 'What shall we do? What shall we say?'

claims.quote: A minairó (Catalan pronunciation: [minəjˈɾo], plural minairons), also called manairó, menairó, diablorí in Catalonia or zaingorriak in the Basque country, is a tiny mythological being that some people save enclosed within a needle tube in some villages of the Pyrenees.

statement.id: Minairó (jamak minairons), juga manairó, menairó, diablorí di Katalonia atau zaingorriak di negeri Basque, adalah makhluk mitis mungil yang di beberapa desa Pyrenees disimpan dalam tabung jarum.
statement.en: A minairó (plural minairons), also manairó, menairó, diablorí in Catalonia or zaingorriak in the Basque Country, is a tiny mythical being that some people keep shut in a needle case in villages of the Pyrenees.

claims.quote: The minairons come from the perforate St John's-wort which blooms at the Saint John’s (the summer solstice) night. It grows in very deep caves guarded by giants and dragons and it only can be caught in the point of midnight on St. John’s Day.

statement.id: Minairons berasal dari tumbuhan St John's-wort yang mekar pada malam Santo Yohanes (titik balik matahari musim panas), tumbuh di gua sangat dalam yang dijaga raksasa dan naga, dan hanya dapat diambil tepat tengah malam hari Santo Yohanes.
statement.en: Minairons come from St John's-wort, which blooms on St John's Night (the summer solstice), grows in very deep caves guarded by giants and dragons, and can only be taken at midnight on St John's Day.

claims.quote: Others say that they are as a swarm of tiny mosquitoes, almost invisible. Some people prefer to compare them with the bee, because of the noise they do buzzing when left the needles’ tube or cane.

statement.id: Sebagian orang menyebut mereka seperti kawanan nyamuk kecil yang hampir tak terlihat, yang lain membandingkannya dengan lebah karena dengungnya saat keluar dari tabung jarum.
statement.en: Some say they are like a swarm of tiny, almost invisible mosquitoes; others compare them to bees for the buzzing they make leaving the needle case.

claims.quote: No one doubts, however, that they are so tiny that inside the cane there must be thousands and when one foregrounds, eager demands for work, saying, "What will we do? What will we say?”

statement.id: Mereka begitu kecil sehingga ribuan muat dalam tabung, dan begitu keluar mereka menuntut pekerjaan sambil berkata, "Apa yang kita kerjakan? Apa yang kita katakan?"
statement.en: They are so tiny that thousands fit in the case, and when they come out they demand work, saying, 'What shall we do? What shall we say?'

claims.quote: The legend says that many of the screes of the Pyrenees have been works of these goblins, when his master opened the needle tube by mistake or accident

statement.id: Legenda menyebut banyak hamparan batu longsoran di Pyrenees adalah buatan mereka ketika tuannya tidak sengaja membuka tabung jarum.
statement.en: Legend says many of the Pyrenean screes are their work, made when a master opened the needle case by mistake.

claims.quote: A handful of heirs of the Pyrenees main houses have been, on occasion, owners of the cane, through which the house went up like a mushroom.

statement.id: Sejumlah pewaris rumah besar di Pyrenees konon memiliki tabung itu, sehingga rumah mereka makmur dengan cepat.
statement.en: A few heirs of great Pyrenean houses reputedly owned the case, through which their house rose like a mushroom.

claims.quote: Al abrirse el canuto, los minairones salían y decían: què farem?, què direm? -"¿qué haremos, qué diremos?"- y si la persona que lo había abierto no les ordenaba hacer algún trabajo inmediatamente, lo mataban

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, bila tabung dibuka dan pembukanya tidak segera memberi pekerjaan, minairons membunuhnya.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, when the case was opened, if the opener did not set them work at once, the minairons killed him.

claims.quote: Mamarro ou les mamarroak sont des Ireluak ou génies de petite taille issus de la mythologie basque, ils aident les gens dans leurs tâches quotidiennes et protègent la famille dans laquelle ils vivent.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, padanan Basque-nya, mamarro atau mamarroak, adalah roh kecil yang membantu pekerjaan sehari-hari dan melindungi keluarga tempat mereka tinggal.
statement.en: According to the French article, the Basque counterpart, mamarro or mamarroak, are small spirits who help with daily tasks and protect the family they live with.

statement.id: Peri kecil ini juga disebut Galtzagorriak, Prakagorriak, dan Zaingorriak di Ordizia, di antara nama lain.
statement.en: These little elves are also called Galtzagorriak, Prakagorriak and Zaingorriak at Ordizia, among other names.

short_description.id: Pitsen adalah roh penguasa hutan dalam mitologi Tatar Siberia yang dapat membawa keberuntungan atau menyesatkan orang, dan pandai berubah wujud.
short_description.en: Pitsen is the forest spirit-master of Siberian Tatar mythology who can bring luck or lead people astray and is a skilled shapeshifter.

long_description.id: Pitsen adalah roh penguasa hutan dalam mitologi Tatar Siberia, padanan Arçuri dari Chuvash dan Şüräle dari Tatar Volga-Ural. Perannya bertentangan: ia bisa membawa keberuntungan, tetapi juga menyesatkan orang ke belantara. Ia sering menjelma orang tua bertongkat atau hewan seperti kera, tinggal di pondok terbengkalai, dan suka menunggang kuda sambil mengolesi surainya dengan ter.
long_description.en: Pitsen is the forest spirit-master of Siberian Tatar mythology, a counterpart of the Chuvash Arçuri and the Volga-Ural Tatar Şüräle. Its role is contradictory: it can bring luck but also lead people into the wilderness. It often appears as an old man with a staff or as animals such as apes, lives in derelict lodges and likes to ride horses and smear their manes with tar.

long_description.id: Dalam wujud gadis cantik, Pitsen dapat menikahi manusia. Menurut satu legenda, seorang pemburu menikahi gadis hutan dan menjadi kaya, sampai ia pulang lebih awal dan melihat monster bergading memakan kadal; begitu ia menjerit, istri dan kekayaannya lenyap.
long_description.en: As a beautiful maiden, Pitsen can marry humans. In one legend a hunter married a forest maiden and grew rich, until he came home early and saw a tusked monster eating lizards; when he cried out, his wife and wealth vanished.

role.en: Brings luck or leads people astray.

did_you_know.en: Pitsen likes to ride horses and smear their manes with tar.

short_description.id: Pearlin Jean adalah hantu yang konon menghantui halaman Allanbank di Allanton, Berwickshire, Skotlandia.
short_description.en: Pearlin Jean is a ghost said to haunt the Allanbank Courtyard at Allanton in Berwickshire, Scotland.

long_description.id: Pearlin Jean adalah nama hantu yang konon menghantui halaman Allanbank di Allanton, Berwickshire, Skotlandia, bekas lokasi rumah janda di tanah milik Blackadder House yang kini sudah dirobohkan. Namanya berasal dari renda "pearlin" yang menutupi tubuhnya menurut para saksi. Menurut legenda ia berasal dari Paris, kekasih Sir Robert Stewart (diangkat Baronet pada 1684). Saat Stewart pulang ke Skotlandia, Jean menghadang keretanya; Stewart menyuruh kusir terus melaju, dan roda kereta melindas dahinya hingga ia tewas. Kata-kata terakhirnya: "Aku akan tiba di Skotlandia sebelum kamu."
long_description.en: Pearlin Jean is the name of a ghost said to haunt the Allanbank Courtyard at Allanton, Berwickshire, Scotland, once the site of a dower house on the estate of the since-demolished Blackadder House. Witnesses gave her the name because she appeared clothed in 'pearlin' lace. Legend makes her a woman from Paris and the lover of Sir Robert Stewart, created a Baronet in 1684. When Stewart left for Scotland she stood in front of his carriage; he told the driver to keep going and the wheels crushed her forehead. Her final words were, 'I'll be in Scotland before you.'

long_description.id: Ketika pertama kali kembali ke tanah miliknya, sebelum 1697, Stewart melihatnya duduk di atas gerbang dengan darah menutupi kepala dan bahunya. Tujuh pendeta setempat gagal mengusirnya. Hantu itu membanting pintu, membuka jendela dan berjalan di rumah siang malam; lama-kelamaan wujudnya menjadi kerangka berbalut renda. Pada abad ke-18 Thomas Blackadder ketakutan saat menemuinya, dan pada 1790 para tamu perempuan terganggu suara langkah kaki. Legendanya diabadikan dalam lagu pada abad ke-19.
long_description.en: On Stewart's first return to the estate, before 1697, he saw her perched above the gateway with blood covering her head and shoulders. Seven local ministers failed to exorcise her. The ghost banged doors, opened windows and roamed the house at all hours, and in time took the form of a skeleton in lace. In the 18th century Thomas Blackadder was terrified on meeting her, and in 1790 lady guests were troubled by pacing footsteps. A 19th-century song preserved the legend.

did_you_know.id: Pearlin Jean dinamai menurut renda yang menutupi tubuhnya dalam penampakan.
did_you_know.en: Pearlin Jean is named after the lace that covers her in sightings.

claims.quote: Pearlin Jean is the name given to a ghost, who purportedly haunts the Allanbank Courtyard, situated in Allanton, Berwickshire, Scotland. The courtyard was previously the site of a dower house called Allanbank of the country estate of the now demolished Blackadder House.

statement.id: Pearlin Jean, hantu di halaman Allanbank (Allanbank Courtyard), Allanton, Berwickshire, Skotlandia (Scotland); bekas rumah janda tanah Blackadder House.
statement.en: Pearlin Jean, a ghost of the Allanbank Courtyard, Allanton, Berwickshire, Scotland; former dower house of Blackadder House.

statement.en: The ghost slammed doors and opened windows; later a skeleton in Pearlin lace; seven ministers failed to exorcise it.

claims.quote: In the 1700s, Thomas Blackadder was said to be infatuated with the figure of Pearlin Jean, and went to meet her in the courtyard. As soon as he realised the nature of the woman, he became incredibly frightened.

short_description.id: Sihirtia (Sirtia) adalah bangsa mitos bertubuh sangat pendek dalam folklor Nenets yang tinggal di tundra sebelum kedatangan orang Nenets.
short_description.en: The Sihirtia (Sirtia) are a mythical, very short people of Nenets folklore who lived in the tundra before the Nenets came.

long_description.id: Sihirtia (Nenets: сихиртя) atau Sirtia (сиртя) adalah bangsa mitos yang mendiami tundra sebelum kedatangan orang Nenets, dan namanya sering muncul dalam folklor Nenets. Menurut legenda mereka sangat pendek, berpakaian indah dengan liontin logam, dan tinggal di bukit pasir tinggi. Mereka keluar ke permukaan tundra pada malam hari atau saat berkabut; di bawah tanah mereka bepergian dengan anjing dan menggembalakan mamut ("rusa tanah"). Artikel ru menyebut mereka takut cahaya siang.
long_description.en: The Sihirtia (Nenets сихиртя) or Sirtia (сиртя) were a mythical people who held the tundra before the Nenets arrived, and they figure often in Nenets folklore. Legend makes them very short, finely dressed with metal pendants, and living in tall sandy hills. They emerged on the tundra at night or in fog; underground they rode on dogs and herded mammoths, the 'earth deer'. The ru article adds that they fear daylight.

long_description.id: Sihirtia adalah pandai besi yang terampil dan prajurit yang baik; bertemu mereka membawa sial atau untung, dan ada kisah pernikahan antara orang Nenets dan Sihirtia. Gambaran folklor ini mungkin menyimpan ciri bangsa nyata, kemungkinan berasal dari rumpun Samoyed atau Paleo-Siberia, yang tinggal di tundra Eropa dan Siberia Barat pada zaman kuno.
long_description.en: The Sihirtia were able smiths and good fighters; meeting one brought either bad or good luck, and Nenets and Sihirtia are said to have intermarried. The folk image may preserve traits of an actual people, perhaps Samoyedic or Paleo-Siberian, who lived in the European and West Siberian tundra in ancient times.

did_you_know.id: Dalam legenda Nenets, Sihirtia menggembalakan mamut di bawah tanah dan menyebutnya "rusa tanah".
did_you_know.en: In Nenets legend the Sihirtia herd mammoths underground, calling them 'earth deer'.

short_description.id: Spiriduș adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Rumania yang menjadi perantara antara tuan rumah dan Iblis, atau makhluk kecil mirip elf yang tinggal di rongga pohon.
short_description.en: The spiriduș is a being of Romanian mythology that mediates between a householder and the Devil, or a tiny elf-like creature living in tree hollows.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Rumania, setelah dipanggil spiriduș menjadi pesuruh atau perantara antara tuan rumah tempat ia lahir dan Iblis; sang tuan dapat meminta keinginan duniawi apa pun kepada Iblis lewat spiriduș, dengan imbalan jiwanya di akhirat. Dalam beberapa dongeng mereka melayani para penyihir.
long_description.en: In Romanian myth, once a spiriduș is summoned it serves as go-between for the master of the house where it was born and the Devil; through it the master can ask the Devil for any earthly wish, paying with his soul in the afterlife. In some tales spiridușii serve sorcerers.

long_description.en: Another picture makes the spiriduș a being like a human but many times smaller, akin to an elf or gnome, living in tree hollows and among the roots of flowers and grasses. They can be wicked or kind, live in large groups, are fine craftsmen, know the secrets of buried treasure and understand the speech of plants and animals. short_description.id: Domba Tumbuhan Tartaria adalah tumbuhan legendaris Asia Tengah yang dipercaya berbuah domba hidup yang tersambung lewat tali pusar, legenda yang berakar pada tanaman kapas.
short_description.en: The Vegetable Lamb of Tartary is a legendary plant of Central Asia believed to bear live sheep tied to it by an umbilical cord, a legend rooted in the cotton plant.

long_description.id: Domba Tumbuhan Tartaria atau Agnus scythicus adalah zoofit legendaris Asia Tengah yang dipercaya berbuah domba. Domba itu terhubung ke tumbuhan oleh tangkai seperti tali pusar, merumput di sekitarnya, dan mati bila rumput habis. Ia dipercaya berdarah, bertulang, dan berdaging seperti domba; darahnya manis seperti madu, wolnya dipakai untuk pakaian, dan hanya serigala yang memangsanya.
long_description.en: The Vegetable Lamb of Tartary or Agnus scythicus is a legendary zoophyte of Central Asia believed to bear sheep. The lamb, tied to the plant by a cord-like stalk, grazes around it and dies when the grass runs out. It was thought to have blood, bones and flesh like a lamb; its blood was sweet as honey, its wool made into clothes, and only wolves preyed on it.

long_description.id: Legenda ini berakar pada kapas, yang belum dikenal di Eropa utara; Herodotos sudah menulis tentang pohon berbuah wol di India, dan Yeduah dalam cerita rakyat Yahudi tercatat sejak 436 M. Odorico sekitar 1314 menulis tentang melon yang melahirkan anak domba, Thomas Browne menyebutnya Boramez, dan nama barometz berasal dari kata Tatar untuk anak domba. Pada masa Renaisans ia banyak dibahas dalam teks filsafat dan botani.
long_description.en: The legend is rooted in cotton, then unknown in northern Europe; Herodotus already wrote of wool-bearing trees in India, and the Yeduah of Jewish folklore is recorded from AD 436. Odoric around 1314 wrote of a lamb-bearing melon, Thomas Browne called it the Boramez, and the name barometz comes from the Tatar for little lamb. In the Renaissance it was much discussed in philosophical and botanical texts.

famous_for.en: The lamb on its umbilical stalk.

note.id: Tumbuhan-hewan serupa dalam cerita rakyat Yahudi.
note.en: A similar plant-animal of Jewish folklore.

statement.en: The Vegetable Lamb of Tartary (Latin Agnus scythicus or Planta Tartarica Barometz) is a legendary zoophyte of Central Asia believed to bear sheep as fruit; the sheep, tied to the plant by an umbilical cord, grazed around it, and when the foliage was gone both died.

short_description.id: Wild haggis adalah makhluk rekaan jenaka dalam cerita rakyat Skotlandia, konon asli Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia dan menjadi sumber hidangan haggis.
short_description.en: The wild haggis is a humorous fictional creature of Scottish folklore, said to be native to the Highlands and the source of the dish haggis.

long_description.id: Wild haggis (dengan nama taksonomi jenaka Haggis scoticus) adalah makhluk rekaan cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore) yang konon asli Dataran Tinggi Skotlandia (Scottish Highlands). Secara bercanda ia diklaim sebagai sumber haggis, hidangan tradisional Skotlandia yang sebenarnya dibuat dari jeroan domba seperti jantung, paru-paru, dan hati. Menurut sebagian sumber, kaki kiri dan kanannya berbeda panjang, seperti sidehill gouger dan dahu, sehingga ia dapat berlari cepat mengelilingi gunung dan lereng terjal habitatnya, tetapi hanya ke satu arah.
long_description.en: The wild haggis (jokingly classified as Haggis scoticus) is a made-up creature of Scottish folklore, supposedly native to the Scottish Highlands. It is claimed in jest to be where haggis comes from, though that traditional Scottish dish is really made from sheep's innards such as heart, lungs and liver. Some say its left and right legs differ in length, like those of the sidehill gouger and the dahu, so it can race round the steep mountains and slopes it lives on, but only one way.

long_description.id: Konon ada dua varietas haggis, satu berkaki kiri lebih panjang dan satu berkaki kanan lebih panjang, yang berlari searah atau berlawanan arah jarum jam mengelilingi gunung. Keduanya hidup damai tetapi tak dapat kawin silang di alam liar, karena jantan harus berbalik menghadap arah yang sama dengan betina dan kehilangan keseimbangan. Menurut survei daring yang dipesan produsen haggis Hall's of Broxburn pada 2003, sepertiga pengunjung AS ke Skotlandia percaya wild haggis makhluk nyata. Menurut artikel de, ia digambarkan sebagai hewan kecil berbulu mirip persilangan kelinci dan tupai.
long_description.en: There are said to be two varieties, one with longer left legs and one with longer right legs, running clockwise or anticlockwise round a mountain. They live in peace but cannot interbreed in the wild, since a male would have to turn to face the female's way and lose his balance. In an online survey commissioned by haggis maker Hall's of Broxburn in 2003, a third of US visitors to Scotland believed the wild haggis was real. According to the de article it is pictured as a small furry animal like a cross between a rabbit and a squirrel.
